newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LUYT WANTS LIONS TO JOIN NATIONS SERIES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LUYT WANTS LIONS TO JOIN NATIONS SERIES.

text.p: South African rugby union president Louis Luyt wants to involve the British Lions in the southern hemisphere Tri-Nations series alongside New Zealand, Australia and South Africa.

"It would be wonderful to see the Lions joining the Tri-Nations series but I realise that because our seasons are so different that may be difficult," Luyt, president of the South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) said on Sunday.

Addressing the Lions on their arrival in South Africa, Luyt, said, "It's vital for everyone in rugby for the Lions concept to remain alive. We want to sit down and talk about structures because we want to see you more often."

Minister of sport Steve Tshwete, a former political prisoner with Nelson Mandela, said: "I was imprisoned on Robben Island in 1974 and the Lions' successful tour gave us all a big boost because in those days we didn't want South Africa to win.
"But things have changed now and the country has rallied behind the Springboks and we hope that your presence will be a boost for rugby in this country."
Lions' manager Fran Cotton said: "History tells us we have a tough task ahead of us and that is the challenge of being a Lion in South Africa.

"Comparisons with the unbeaten team of 1974 are irrelevant because we are here to create our own sense of history but if there is one similarity between that side and this one it is that there is already a terrific feeling of unity among the players."

Coach Ian McGeechan said, "It's a great challenge for us to become part of the culture which produced the Super 12 because we've seen some wonderful rugby in that competition. But equally it would be nice one day for the Lions to be able to play South Africa or New Zealand in the northern hemisphere."

The Lions will spend five days in Umhlanga, a coastal resort north of Durban, before flying down to Port Elizabeth where their first match will be against an Eastern Province Invitation XI. The three tests are in Cape Town on June 21, Durban on June 28 and Johannesburg on July 5.
